paragraphs.source_en: "Ah," said Stendahl, eyes closed. He shoved the last brick into place and mortared it tight. "_Requiescat in pace_, dear friend." He hastened from the catacomb. In the seven rooms the sound of a midnight clock brought everything to a halt. The Red Death appeared. Stendahl turned for a moment at the door to watch. And then he ran out of the great House, across the moat, to where a helicopter waited. "Ready, Pikes?" "Ready." "There it goes!" They looked at the great House, smiling. It began to crack down the middle, as with an earthquake, and as Stendahl watched the magnificent sight he heard Pikes reading behind him in a low, cadenced voice: "'. . . my brain reeled as I saw the mighty walls rushing asunder--there was a long tumultuous shouting sound like the voice of a thousand waters--and the deep and dank tarn at my feet closed sullenly and silently over the fragments of the House of Usher.'" The helicopter rose over the steaming lake and flew into the west.
